narration: The concrete under your feet already finished polluting, before the building even opened.
Here's why. Cement is made by heating limestone in a kiln, at around fourteen hundred and fifty degrees, and that chemistry alone releases carbon dioxide.
Add the steel in the frame, and together they produce around fifteen percent of global CO2.
That's roughly seven times all of aviation, at about two percent.
And it all happens before day one. This is embodied carbon, and most net zero marketing leaves it out. Solar panels make a better photo than a spreadsheet about fly ash.
The fix already exists. Blended cements with fly ash or slag, mass timber where it fits, and recycled steel.
Nobody in a finished lobby asks what the concrete used to be. Now you will.
